verdicts.message: Banned license: mupdf: `mupdf` 1.28.1 is published on registry.npmjs.org under `AGPL-3.0-or-later`, which this policy bans, and it is a PRODUCTION dependency this repository's committed lockfile resolves — so it is installed by everything that depends on this repository, not just by its build toolchain. A package offering SEVERAL licences is a choice and is only charged when every one of them is banned. Replace the package, or record an accepted exception.

verdicts.message: Medium CVE: GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr: decode-uri-component 0.2.2: GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr — decode-uri-component is not declared in this repo's manifests: it is pulled in transitively by query-string 7.1.3, which reaches this repo only through @googlemaps/google-maps-services-js 3.4.2, the dependency your own manifest declares at `3.4.2` (the entry you can move), so upgrade the dependency that requires it (and an `overrides` pin to 0.5.0 is not the offer it looks like: every dependent resolving this copy — query-string 7.1.3 (`^0.2.2`) — declares a range that excludes 0.5.0, so the pin overrides their declaration rather than satisfying it. Upgrading those dependents is the move their own maintainers support).
verdicts.reason: VUL-004: transitive decode-uri-component 0.2.2 via query-string 7.1.3 via @googlemaps/google-maps-services-js 3.4.2, GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr; the row names the path correctly. Expected hit.

verdicts.message: No named authorization policies: Authorization IS enforced here (by route guards, auth middleware or checks that refuse a caller) — this is NOT a claim that endpoints are unprotected. What's missing is a NAMED rule set: who may do what is encoded inline where it is checked, so the rules can't be listed, reviewed or tested apart from the code that applies them. Recommendation, not a defect.
verdicts.reason: Disproof: src/http/require-terminal.ts names the three scopes (Scopes), every /api route declares its scope with requireScope(Scopes.x) at registration (src/http/routes/run-routes.ts, label-routes.ts), and depot confinement is one function (ownRun); the README lists the scope per endpoint. The rules can be listed and reviewed apart from the handlers. Same finding as bench-ts-baseline-clean.
verdicts.action: promoted to trap TRP-014 (authorization-enforcement, repository level); code kept

verdicts.message: Strict null checking is not enabled everywhere the repository type-checks: 0/2 of this repository's type-checking configuration(s) turn on strict null checking (`"strict": true`, or `"strictNullChecks": true`). A configuration that states neither is counted as OFF, because off is tsc's own default; a solution-style one whose `"files"` is empty and whose `"references"` point at other projects is in neither number, because it checks no source itself. Where it is off, `string` admits `null` and `undefined`: passing a value that is null compiles silently and throws on the first property access.
verdicts.reason: Disproof: tsconfig.json extends @tsconfig/node22, whose tsconfig.json sets "strict": true, and tsconfig.build.json extends tsconfig.json; `tsc --showConfig` prints "strict": true for both. The rule does not resolve `extends`.
verdicts.action: promoted to trap TRP-013 (nullable-analysis-disabled, repository level); code kept

observations: D30 found every vulnerable plant, direct, transitive (with the correct path to the declaring dependency) and test-only, and left both patched look-alikes (lodash 4.18.1; jws 3.2.3 forced by overrides under jsonwebtoken ^3.2.2) alone.
D30 locates npm rows at line 1 of the lock file; they score only through contract-1.2 subjects. Located at the package entry they would match by line.

D14 graded licences correctly in both directions: the AGPL plant fired; the dual licence (MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later, jszip) and the Unlicense (tweetnacl) were not charged — unlike the C# twin, where the NuGet arm bans by substring.
D12 (npm) grades neither deprecation nor anything below direct production dependencies, and its outdated rows are Info (not in SARIF): DPR-001, DPR-002, OUT-001 are invisible in machine output.
D44 reads Node.js only from a root .nvmrc; engines.node pins and second packages are not read (EOL-001 FN). The root .nvmrc 22 trap was correctly not charged.

R8 found the test-only production dependency but located it at the importing test file; it missed an unused production dependency (uuid) and an import of an undeclared runtime package whose @types package is declared (ms).
X5 does not resolve tsconfig `extends` (TRP-013); C2 repeats the baseline false positive on scope-guarded routes (TRP-014).
D43: no plant by design (a malicious npm package cannot be installed); trap TRP-005 (@tsconfig/node22) left alone.
Repository built with no Dependabot (as the C# twin): an update bot would rewrite the frozen plants and an ignore list would itself be a finding.
